models.title: Days of sales outstanding
models.summary: Days of sales outstanding divides the reporting-period duration by its corresponding turnover.

relationship.original_equation: Days of sales outstanding = period length / matching turnover
relationship.translation_notes: Period is a physical duration in days, not an annualization factor; output retains the same duration unit. Turnover is a dimensionless count over that period.

variables.definition: Physical length of the reporting period
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Receivables turnover for the reporting period, calculated consistently from either total revenue or credit sales and average receivables
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Days of sales outstanding as an elapsed duration
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Turnover and period duration cover the same entity, accounting period and averaging convention.
A year can contain 365, 366 or another number of days; it is supplied rather than hard-coded.
The turnover basis is explicitly identified: the financial-analysis module uses total revenue, while the corporate-issuer module specifies credit sales.
limitations: Turnover is an accounting approximation and does not identify the actual holding time of each individual item.
Zero turnover has no finite duration in this model.
Total-sales and credit-sales versions can yield different days; credit-sales turnover can feed this formula only when the scopes of receivables and period match.
